div.style: color: rgb(16, 42, 67) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 345px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(11, 60, 82) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 345px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(6, 64, 43) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 345px; text-align: center;

span.p: A seam between parts

div.style: color: rgb(90, 58, 0) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 345px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(92, 34, 6) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 345px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(74, 59, 0) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 345px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(79, 36, 67) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 345px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(16, 42, 67) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 345px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Protein sequence → ESM-C 600M
One amino-acid string per target; median 454
residues, longest 34,350. Out comes one vector
per residue, from 573,632,640 frozen weights:
572 effective target units cannot fine-tune a
model this size without fitting the targets
rather than the binding.

div.style: color: rgb(16, 42, 67) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 345px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Residue cache · 14.0 GiB
All 10,820 targets encoded once.
Reproduces bit-for-bit, which is
what makes reuse safe.

div.style: color: rgb(11, 60, 82) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 345px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Ligand SMILES → line graph + knowledge
One standardised string per molecule, rewritten so
each bond is a node. Two extra nodes hold a
512-bit fingerprint and 200 computed properties.

div.style: color: rgb(11, 60, 82) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 345px; text-align: center;

span.p:
LiGhT · 8 layers, 8 heads, width 96
Each bond looks at bonds up to five
atoms away. Bond-to-bond attention
is kept for iBAM.

div.style: color: rgb(11, 60, 82) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 345px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Summary → 288
Fingerprint node, property node, mean
over bonds — never blended.

div.style: color: rgb(11, 60, 82) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 345px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Pre-training · done
Hide one knowledge node, rebuild it
from the molecule plus the other.

540,166 molecules — training-only,
so held-out sets and sealed panels
are excluded.

Held-out loss 0.2002, 48.8% under
a molecule-blind guess.

div.style: color: rgb(6, 64, 43) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 345px; text-align: center; width: 345px;

span.p:
The seam: what the ligand hands over
One vector per bond, plus two masks — one for what is real rather than padding,
one for what may be drawn on a molecule. The knowledge nodes are real but not
drawable, and conflating those two questions is what forced them to be discarded before.

div.style: color: rgb(11, 60, 82) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 345px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Protein → 96
1152 per residue, narrowed.

div.style: color: rgb(11, 60, 82) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 345px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Bonds → 96
96 per bond, normalised.

div.style: color: rgb(11, 60, 82) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 345px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Summary → 3 × 96
Each part projected on its own, so the
fingerprint is never averaged in with
the properties.

div.style: color: rgb(90, 58, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 345px; text-align: center; width: 345px;

span.p:
Knowledge conditioning · FiLM · 74,496
The molecule's global properties rescale every residue and every bond instead of
being appended at the end — appended can be ignored, multiplied cannot. Starts as an
exact no-op, so switching it off compares the same model, not a different random draw.

div.style: color: rgb(11, 60, 82) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 345px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Protein looks at ligand
Each residue spreads attention over the
molecule's bonds. 96 → 192 → 96.

div.style: color: rgb(51, 51, 51) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 345px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Two separate sets of weights, side by
side. Neither sees the other's output,
and one is not the transpose of the other.

div.style: color: rgb(11, 60, 82) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 345px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Ligand looks at protein
Each bond spreads attention over the
residues. 96 → 192 → 96.

div.style: color: rgb(11, 60, 82) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 345px; text-align: center; width: 345px;

span.p:
One vector for the pair · 576 numbers, six blocks
Fused residues · fused bonds · the protein before fusion · fingerprint · properties · bond average.
The pre-fusion block is a route to an answer that does not need attention to have found anything.

div.style: color: rgb(11, 60, 82) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 345px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(11, 60, 82) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 345px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(11, 60, 82) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 345px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(92, 34, 6) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 345px; text-align: center; width: 345px;

span.p:
Score only the endpoint that was measured
Kd, Ki and IC50 are different experiments and are never mixed. A measurement that
does not exist cannot be given a stand-in value — no such value is representable.

div.style: color: rgb(74, 59, 0) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 345px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Exact
Error under the lab's own repeat
scatter is free: 0.945 Kd, 0.641 Ki,
0.671 IC50.

div.style: color: rgb(74, 59, 0) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 345px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Censored · 16.6%
'Weaker than 10 µM'. Penalised for
crossing the bound, never for landing
inside it.

div.style: color: rgb(74, 59, 0) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 345px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Lower-confidence
Weighted 0.25 and kept structurally
apart, so they cannot reach the
main term.

div.style: color: rgb(74, 59, 0) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 345px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Which of two is better
Built, off by default. Inside one assay
only, and only when the gap beats that
endpoint's repeat scatter.

div.style: color: rgb(51, 51, 51) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 345px; text-align: center;

span.p:
iBAM — what the model looked at
Every map kept per layer and per head,
unaveraged: 32 protein-ligand, 64 bond-bond.

Residue × bond is native, because a token
is a bond. Residue × atom is derived and
labelled so.

Rows sum to one, so rows rank nothing —
columns are the orderable direction.

div.style: color: rgb(11, 60, 82) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 345px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Ensemble
Three separately trained models.
Three passes over one model is
refused in code.

div.style: color: rgb(11, 60, 82) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 345px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Calibrated intervals
Split conformal on a held-apart slice.
Too few points returns a status, never
an invented interval.

div.style: color: rgb(11, 60, 82) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 345px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Is this input familiar?
Similarity to training molecules only —
an ensemble can agree confidently
about the unseen.

div.style: color: rgb(92, 34, 6) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 345px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Benchmark lock
Refuses to score on the sealed panels when
training overlaps them. Measured, not guessed
from the split's name: random 60–100%,
cold-target 66–69%, time-based 0% — the only
one that qualifies. Opening cannot be undone.

div.style: color: rgb(51, 51, 51) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 345px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Drug fishing — an evaluation, not a part
3,721 targets · 81,971 actives · 37,187 measured
inactives · 1,926,939 matched decoys. A question
asked of a finished model, so it needs no tower.

div.style: color: rgb(79, 36, 67) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 345px; text-align: center;

span.p:
What it would be told
Target, endpoint, seed molecule,
what the model attended to, and
the scaffold to preserve.

div.style: color: rgb(79, 36, 67) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 345px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Discrete graph diffusion
Atoms and bonds corrupted to noise
by category and denoised back,
scaffold held fixed.

div.style: color: rgb(79, 36, 67) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 345px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Back to a real molecule
RDKit decode, sanitise, scaffold
re-checked by atom mapping.
Validity reported before and after.

div.style: color: rgb(92, 34, 6) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 345px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Never shown the answer it predicts.
Sampling is not differentiable, so
gradients stop here.

div.style: color: rgb(79, 36, 67) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 345px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Planned: the full objective
Affinity + ranking + generation +
measured-change. Only affinity and
ranking exist today.
